cards.text: This song belongs to David, the shepherd who became king of Israel. Its title ties it to the time he pretended to be insane before Abimelech, and the king drove him away. Getting run out of a room is rough, friend, and I say that as a stamper who got slid into the back of a junk drawer.

cards.question: In a song tied to a moment like that, what does David say he'll do at all times?

cards.text: David says his soul boasts in the LORD. Most bragging clears a room, but this is bragging about the LORD, and that's a whole different thing.

cards.question: David wants the ___ to hear his boasting in the LORD and rejoice.
David wants to praise the LORD on his own, with nobody else joining in.

cards.text: Then David tells his own story: "I sought the LORD, and He answered me". I bet his heart was pounding back there before Abimelech.

cards.question: David says the LORD delivered him from all his ___.
David says the faces of those who look to the LORD will end up covered in shame.

cards.text: Then David talks about "This poor man" who called out, and the LORD heard him. Poor man? Baker, I came out of a closing-down bakery's bin with a 25 cent sticker on me, so I'm the poor man's POOR MAN.

cards.question: The LORD saved this poor man from just some of his troubles.

cards.text: Next, David says the angel of the LORD sets up camp, and he delivers. Meanwhile my whole security team in the junk drawer was a twist tie and the dead batteries I shared that drawer with.

cards.question: Where does David say the angel of the LORD encamps?

cards.text: Then David hands out an invitation, and he doesn't say hear about it. He says TASTE, and baker, I have been telling people that about cookies my WHOLE LIFE.

cards.question: David invites people to taste and see what about the LORD?

cards.text: David says blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him. Then he turns to the LORD's saints and tells them to fear Him.

cards.question: David tells the saints that those who fear the LORD lack ___.

cards.text: Then David brings in young lions. Strong, fast, built for the hunt, and if ANYBODY in this song should be set for life, it's them.

cards.question: What does David say happens to those young lions?
David says the young lions end up better off than those who seek the LORD.

cards.text: Now David switches hats and becomes the teacher. He says, "Come, children, listen to me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD."
Then David asks who delights in life and wants to see good days. Friend, that's everybody who ever hit snooze hoping TODAY would finally be the good one.

cards.question: For anyone who wants good days, what's the first thing David tells them to do?

cards.text: David starts with the mouth, no evil and no deceitful speech, and friend, I have tried snatching a sent message back out of the air. You CAN'T.

cards.question: David says to sit back and wait for peace to come find you.

cards.text: Turn from evil, do good, chase peace down. Then David says the eyes of the LORD are on the righteous.

cards.question: The LORD's eyes are on the righteous. What does David say His ears are inclined to?

cards.text: But for those who do evil, David says the face of the LORD is against them.

cards.question: David says the memory of those who do evil will live on forever on the earth.

cards.text: Then David says the righteous cry out, the LORD hears, and He delivers them from all their troubles. Sounds a lot like that poor man from earlier, doesn't it?

cards.question: Who does David say the LORD is near to?
David says the righteous won't face any afflictions at all.

cards.text: And for the righteous man, David says the LORD protects all his bones, and not one of them will be broken. Baker, I've been dropped, slid across a kitchen and buried under takeout menus, and I would LOVE that kind of coverage.

cards.question: David says ___ will slay the wicked.

cards.text: David adds that the haters of the righteous will be condemned. But he doesn't end the song there, because he's got one more word about the LORD's servants.

cards.question: The LORD ___ His servants, and none who take ___ in Him will be condemned.

findings.problem: The card introduces David as 'the shepherd who became king of Israel.' That fact comes from outside the passage (1 Samuel 16; 2 Samuel 5), but the card cites only Psalm 34:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The right answer 'Bless the LORD' sounds like Scripture. Both wrong answers are modern idioms ('Watch his back', 'Keep his head down'), so the right answer stands out by tone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: 'I bet his heart was pounding' points straight at fear, and the next card (card 7) asks what the LORD delivered David from, with 'fears' as the answer. The setup line also rules out 'enemies' and 'sins'.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Then David talks about...', 'Poor man?' and 'Baker, I came out of...'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke adds new backstory. Nothing in the backstory says he was ever 'dropped.' Saying he was 'slid across a kitchen' also contradicts the backstory, where he was carried across the kitchen and slid into the drawer.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: No story card sets up the turn to what happens to the wicked. The card before talks about the righteous man's bones. With nothing to reason from, 'evil' versus 'war' or 'sickness' is a guess at the wording of the line.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Blank 2 ('take ___ in Him', answer 'refuge') repeats a phrase from Psalm 34:8, which stop 1 card 15 already told ('blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him'). An earlier card gives this answer away, and the phrase is being asked about the second time it appears.

rule.text: When a line repeats, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears.

findings.problem: The question types in stop 2 follow a strict alternating pattern for the first six choice cards (multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false, multiple choice, true or false), then two fill in the blanks in a row.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.
